**Indikator 4a2** is a secondary healthcare quality indicator in Denmark designed to measure the sustained treatment coverage of patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) over time [^src1]. While primary indicators might look at initial treatment, Indikator 4a2 specifically evaluates the proportion of AF patients with an indication for [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] who are still receiving this treatment two years after their index date [^src1]. It is a key component of the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram's (RKKP) annual quality monitoring, working in tandem with Indikator 4a1 (which measures one-year coverage) to ensure long-term adherence to national clinical guidelines [^src1].

The established quality standard for Indikator 4a2 requires that at least 90% of eligible patients receive treatment [^src1]. During the measurement period spanning from July 1, 2021, to June 30, 2022, the national performance across [[danmark|Danmark]] fell slightly short of this goal, achieving a coverage rate of 88.6% (95% CI: 88.0–89.3) [^src1]. 

Performance varied across different administrative levels, highlighting areas of both success and needed improvement [^src1]. [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] successfully met the national standard with a coverage rate of 91.1% (95% CI: 89.2–92.9), and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] also surpassed the threshold at 90.4% (95% CI: 89.0–91.6) [^src1]. At the local level, [[sundhedsklynge-syd|Sundhedsklynge Syd]] recorded the lowest proportion among the reported clusters at 84.3% (95% CI: 80.6–87.6) [^src1]. By providing this hierarchical breakdown, the indicator enables regions and local health clusters to pinpoint specific weaknesses in their long-term AF management and drive targeted quality improvements [^src1].
